newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran presidential election result formally approved.
newsitem.headline: Iran presidential election result formally approved.

text.p: A powerful state body on Wednesday approved the results of Iran's presidential election in which moderate Mohammad Khatami won a landslide victory, state-run Tehran radio said.

It said the Guardian Council, a 12-member body of lawyers and Shi'ite Moslem clerics that screens candidates and oversees elections, voted to give final approval to Friday's polls in which former culture minister Khatami won 69 percent of the 29.1 million votes cast.
In continuing debate over the election, Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei blasted Western media for suggesting Khatami's election was a protest vote.
"They (Western commentators) said this election was a protest. What protest?...So what are the slogans of the president elected by the people?" Khamenei said in remarks carried by the radio.

"The slogans of the president-elect are law and order, ending discrimination, social justice, moving towards Islamic and revolutionary goals...Are these against the Islamic state system? These are the very slogans of the Islamic system," Khamenei said.
Khatami, a Shi'ite cleric with a reputation as a tolerant politician, won on a platform that included guaranteeing constitutional rights and fighting discrimination against women.
He defeated Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, a conservative candidate backed by a majority of the clerical establishment, and two other candidates.

Speaking to parliament members, Khamenei called for political unity after the election which he said was a victory because of the high voter turnout. Some 33 million of Iran's 60 million people were eligible to vote.

"The enemy wants to turn this into a quarrel...and deprive you of the sweetness of victory. Do not let it succeed. It is time for you to be vigilant," said Khamenei, who outranks the president and has supreme power over all state institutions.
